pages.title: Protect the text your application is about to send
pages.description: Choose the Redact Secret integration that matches the boundary you need to protect.
pages.lede: Start with the boundary you control. You do not need to learn every package before making one path safe.

sections.title: What are you trying to protect?
body: Choose the closest task. Each path leads directly to a minimal example and its honest coverage boundary.

sections.title: One detector, several boundaries
body: Core detects and applies policy. Adapters carry host values to core. Vault adds controlled restoration. Gateway protects a reviewed API subset before forwarding. None of these claims that an empty finding set proves the input is secret-free.

pages.title: Quickstart
pages.description: Choose a JavaScript or Python Redact Secret quickstart and get a first redacted result.
pages.lede: Run the core directly first, then move the same detection boundary into the host integration you actually use.

sections.title: Choose your runtime
body: Both paths use released packages and synthetic input. They return sanitized text plus findings that explain what changed.
bullets: — Node.js and browser-capable core
— the Python core package

sections.title: Then place the boundary
body: If your text already enters through a logger, tracer, tool call, or model-context builder, use the matching adapter instead of rewriting host behavior yourself.

pages.title: Installation
pages.description: Install current Redact Secret packages without copying stale version numbers from prose.
pages.lede: Commands on this site are rendered from the release records used by the rest of the site.

sections.title: JavaScript
body: Install the current core release. Integration guides replace this with the adapter package they need.

sections.title: Python
body: Install the current Python mirror of the core release.

pages.title: JavaScript core
pages.description: Scan and redact application-controlled text with the Redact Secret JavaScript core.
pages.lede: Use the core when your application already owns the text boundary and needs findings and sanitized output directly.

sections.title: Scan and redact
body: Initialize once, pass a string, and use the returned redacted text. The example value is deliberately synthetic.

sections.title: Runtime boundary
body: The package supports Node.js and the browser. Use the web-stream subpath for streaming browser text. Detection does not send input over the network.
bullets: A finding reports byte ranges, detector identity, confidence, and action.
A block or processing failure must stop the caller from forwarding the original value.

pages.title: Python core
pages.description: Scan and redact application-controlled text with the Redact Secret Python package.
pages.lede: Use the Python package when your code owns the value before it reaches a logger, request, store, or model.

sections.title: Scan and redact
body: The result keeps sanitized text and findings together so callers do not need to reconstruct replacements.

sections.title: What the result means
body: Findings are evidence of what the configured detectors saw. No findings is not proof that the input is safe.

pages.title: Protect Pino logs
pages.description: Redact values and finished Pino log lines before they reach the destination stream.
pages.lede: The adapter protects values passed to Pino and the finished line before it reaches the configured destination.

sections.title: Install and attach
body: Install the released adapter and wrap the logger boundary.

sections.title: Coverage
body: Value-based detection complements Pino's path-based redact option.
bullets: Covers values in log calls and the completed line.
Does not redact object keys or anything a destination adds after the line is written.
Detection policy still belongs to Redact Secret core.

pages.title: Protect OpenTelemetry data
pages.description: Redact OpenTelemetry span fields before the next processor and log bodies before export.
pages.lede: Use signal-specific adapters so trace and log contracts remain explicit.

sections.title: Trace adapter
body: Wrap the next SpanProcessor. The adapter sanitizes span names, string attributes, events, links, and status messages before delegation.

sections.title: Coverage and limits
body: Attribute names are not redacted. A span the wrapped processor never receives is outside the boundary. OpenTelemetry logs are a separate beta-channel package.

pages.title: Protect Python logs
pages.description: Add value-based redaction to Python logging handlers with a fail-closed filter.
pages.lede: Attach the filter to every emitting handler so records are sanitized at the output boundary.

sections.title: Install
body: The adapters package follows the Python core release independently.

sections.title: Attach the filter
body: The filter covers only handlers that receive it. Put it on every emitting handler rather than assuming the logger applies it everywhere.

pages.title: Protect MCP tool calls
pages.description: Sanitize MCP tools/call and resources/read results before logging, storage, or model context.
pages.lede: Protect tool results at the client boundary without coupling detection to an MCP SDK implementation.

sections.title: Install
body: The MCP adapter builds on the AI-context boundary and uses released packages.

sections.title: Protect a result
body: The supported boundary covers tools/call and resources/read results and can include tool arguments. Binary or encoded values block by default rather than being decoded speculatively.

pages.title: Protect AI and LLM context
pages.description: Build sanitized model context from user text and tool results with fail-closed behavior.
pages.lede: Use this boundary when your application assembles model-bound text but does not need a protocol-specific adapter.

sections.title: Install
body: The package walks supported text values and delegates every detection decision to core.

sections.title: Build context
body: The transformation is all-or-nothing. Unsupported binary or encoded content blocks the result; model output is outside this input boundary.

pages.title: Protect reviewed API traffic with Gateway
pages.description: Route a supported OpenAI SDK request through the experimental fail-closed Redact Secret Gateway.
pages.lede: Gateway is an unpublished candidate for a bounded OpenAI text subset. It is optional and is not a general proxy or a stable production release.

sections.title: Route the SDK
body: Build the candidate from source, validate its configuration, and point an existing SDK at the loopback endpoint.

sections.title: Fail-closed boundary
body: Supported request bodies are fully admitted, inspected, and transformed before any body bytes are sent upstream.
bullets: Unknown fields, unsupported content, malformed input, exhausted limits, or processing failures are rejected.
Provider responses and upstream errors are relayed without response-content redaction.
No artifact is published, signed, or authorized for production distribution.

pages.title: Restore protected values with Vault
pages.description: Capture sensitive values as opaque tokens and restore them only into an explicitly granted sink and path.
pages.lede: Vault is for workflows that must recover an original value later. Core scanning and redaction do not require it.

sections.title: Capture and restore
body: Capture replaces a value with an opaque token. Restore succeeds only for the granted sink and path.

sections.title: Security semantics
body: In-memory Vault use is beta. Persistent profiles are alpha and supported only for qualified deployment combinations.
bullets: Tokens expire and may be single-use.
Restoration is all-or-nothing for the designated field.
A token is not an authorization grant by itself.

pages.title: Detection, findings, and policy
pages.description: Understand how Redact Secret separates detector evidence from the action applied at a runtime boundary.
pages.lede: Detection reports evidence. Policy decides whether a finding is redacted, blocked, warned, or otherwise handled.

sections.title: Keep the layers separate
body: Adapters and gateways do not decide what a secret is. They carry values into core and enforce the returned result at their boundary.
bullets: Findings identify byte ranges and detector evidence.
Actions describe the configured response.
Overlapping findings are resolved deterministically before replacement.

sections.title: PII is opt-in and bounded
body: Credential detection and PII selection are different controls. PII modes cover documented selectors only; Redact Secret is not a general DLP platform.

pages.title: Supported credentials and status
pages.description: Read Redact Secret credential-family status without copying volatile benchmark numbers into documentation.
lede: credential families. Counts and status come from generated evidence, not this prose.

sections.title: Status words
body: Stable means the documented support claim has the required evidence. Provisional, pending, and unsupported describe different evidence or coverage boundaries; they are not synonyms for unsafe or safe.
bullets: Stable: supported on the stated basis and release.
Provisional: useful behavior exists, but the stable evidence bar is not met.
Pending: tracked but not yet claimed.
Unsupported: explicitly outside the current claim.

sections.title: No finding is not proof
body: An empty finding set means the configured detectors did not report a match. It does not prove the input contains no secret.

pages.title: Security and trust boundary
pages.description: Place Redact Secret at a boundary you control and keep forwarding conditional on a successful sanitized result.
pages.lede: Redaction helps only when the application routes sensitive text through the protected boundary and does not fall back to the original value.

sections.title: Caller responsibilities
body: Treat processing errors and blocked results as stop conditions. Never log diagnostics that echo the input or plaintext findings.
bullets: Restrict bypass paths around the adapter or gateway.
Keep provider credentials separate from model-bound text.
Review downstream destinations that can append their own data after redaction.
Use synthetic examples in tests and support reports.

pages.title: Troubleshooting
pages.description: Diagnose blocked values, missed boundaries, version mismatches, and unsupported Redact Secret inputs.
pages.lede: Start with the boundary and the exact released package versions, then reduce the problem with synthetic input.

sections.title: Common paths
body: Do not paste the original sensitive value into an issue, log, screenshot, or diagnostic.
bullets: Nothing changed: confirm the value actually crosses the wrapped handler, processor, callback, or tool-result boundary.
The request blocked: check for unsupported binary, encoded, structured, or protocol fields before changing policy.
Versions disagree: reinstall the exact current command shown on this site and inspect peer ranges.
A secret was missed: reproduce with an unmistakably synthetic value and compare the configured profile with the support matrix.
A false positive appeared: capture detector identity, action, and safe surrounding structure without the original secret.

sections.title: Escalate securely
body: Potential vulnerabilities and sensitive reports belong in the private security channel, not a public issue.
